fresh_internal_checks.check: The general foundation is placed in Chapter 1; the normalized model application remains in Chapter 15.
The energy lemma assumes a locally bounded real function with locally finite signed measure Laplacian; positivity of that Laplacian is not assumed.
The cutoff is between zero and one and has a compactly contained neighborhood, so its mollified Laplacian total variation is bounded by the original mass there.
Integration by parts for smooth mollifications has the stated sign and two cross terms; Young inequality absorbs half the gradient energy.
Local L2 convergence of the uniformly bounded mollifications identifies the weak Sobolev limit with the original distribution.
The pole-test coordinate ball has compact closure in a larger chart, allowing a uniform smooth lower Hessian correction and upper bound.
Smooth correction and constant subtraction give a negative plurisubharmonic function with unchanged pole set.
Its truncations are bounded subharmonic functions; their positive Laplacian masses are uniformly bounded on the fixed cutoff neighborhood by local L1 norm.
The sharper squared-truncation estimate is linear in the truncation depth times the absolute potential; a quadratic bound would not give vanishing energy.
The mollified Caccioppoli estimate gives cutoff energy at most C times the depth, with C independent of that depth.
Division by the depth gives vanishing full W1,2 norm, including cutoff-gradient and L2 terms.
Upper semicontinuity makes the deep sublevel set an actual open neighborhood of every compact subset of the pole set.
Zero extension and sufficiently small positive mollification give genuine smooth compact tests between zero and one, still one near the compact set, without increasing norm.
Local bounded equivalence gives identical Borel pole sets and a locally bounded difference off that common set.
Pole sets are Lebesgue null because the genuine quasi-psh functions are locally integrable; redefining the difference there does not change its distribution.
Smooth local corrections make the Hessians positive order-zero currents, so the difference has finite signed or complex coefficient measures.
Euclidean trace gives a signed measure Laplacian of the bounded difference, activating the energy lemma.
Every real and imaginary Hessian coefficient is a first derivative of an L2 gradient, hence a continuous local Sobolev functional.
For a compact subset of the pole set in a positive Hahn set, outer regularity makes the negative Jordan mass of the test neighborhood arbitrarily small.
The smooth tests give positive mass of that compact set bounded by the vanishing functional pairing plus the arbitrarily small negative mass.
Inner regularity and the same argument for the negative Jordan part exclude all real and imaginary coefficient measures from the common pole set.
Smooth background coefficients have zero mass on the pole set; coefficientwise current restriction is invariant under smooth coordinate changes.
Bounded equivalence pulls back on every fixed modification, so the comparison genuinely descends to ordinary bounded-difference classes.
The ordinary gauge estimate bounds the projected model plus gauge between the original model plus the two scalar extrema, without a mass assumption.
That estimate gives bounded equivalence to the raw transported model; ordinary-envelope dependence on the class gives the fixed-point and inverse identities directly.
The argument does not invoke unrestricted ordinary-envelope idempotence or the positive-lower-volume theorem.
The raw gauge identity and polar bounded-invariance prove exact preservation of the comparison after normalized model transport, with unchanged positive denominators.
Smooth subtraction and bounded changes retain analytic singularities; the ideal gauge bound and ordinary fixed-point property identify the ideal transported model.
The transformed smooth background need not be Hermitian; genuine transported potentials and equal denominators suffice.
General model separation, simultaneous limit realization, analytic closure, agreement with positive-volume topology and two-sided degeneration remain open.
No claim says that projection of an arbitrary non-model potential preserves its full polar data, and no formal research question is closed.
